chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-La', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no harm with the kohl (eye cosmetic) for the fasting person.

key_terms.الْكُحْلِ: Kohl, a traditional eye cosmetic applied to the eyelids or under the eyes
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies that applying kohl does not break the fast, reflecting the Shia juristic consensus that substances entering the eyes do not reach the stomach in the same manner as food or drink. It highlights the principle of ease in fasting rituals, distinguishing between external application and internal consumption, a key distinction in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the nullifiers of Sawm.
